phases.name: Frame the SLO contract and user surfaces
phases.description: Keep stated targets separate from assumptions, then identify the monitored services, telemetry boundary, and operator surface.

phases.name: Define, ingest, and evaluate SLIs
phases.description: Version SLO definitions and service-chain membership, compute windowed budgets from durable events, and keep forecast evaluation evidence.

phases.name: Connect the measurement and prediction path
phases.description: Wire telemetry into a continuously updated evaluator and train/serve breach forecasts from historical, time-correct data.

phases.name: Close the mitigation and reporting loop
phases.description: Route predictions through guarded actions, keep dashboards current, and verify accuracy, latency, coverage, and customer reporting.

steps.phase: Frame the SLO contract and user surfaces
steps.title: Read the frozen brief as acceptance criteria
steps.content: The brief requires live SLI/SLO monitoring, continuously updated error budgets, breach forecasts 1–4 hours ahead with confidence, service/team compliance, customer reports, guarded automated mitigation, and composite service-chain SLAs. Its explicit constraints are under one-minute monitoring latency, greater than 90% breach-prediction accuracy, at least 500 SLO definitions, hourly/daily/monthly windows, and real-time dashboard updates. These are targets to demonstrate, not properties this diagram can guarantee.

steps.phase: Frame the SLO contract and user surfaces
steps.title: Leave missing sizing and evaluation details explicit
steps.content: The brief does not state telemetry volume, tenant count, retention, availability, or the exact accuracy metric and evaluation cohort. Do not invent them: ask for these in the interview, and define the forecast horizon, labels, confidence calibration, and latency measurement boundary before claiming the stated targets are met.

steps.phase: Frame the SLO contract and user surfaces
steps.title: Represent monitored services as the source of evidence
steps.content: Treat the service fleet as the systems being observed and, only after explicit policy approval, possible mitigation targets. Give each emitted observation a service/team identity and event time so compliance can be attributed without confusing ingestion time with occurrence time.

component.label: Monitored Services
component.description: Existing services emit identifiable SLI telemetry and expose narrowly scoped, policy-approved mitigation interfaces; service and team ownership are retained with each observation.

properties.purpose: Existing services emit identifiable SLI telemetry and expose narrowly scoped, policy-approved mitigation interfaces; service and team ownership are retained with each observation.

component.highlightReason: The system observes existing services; it should not assume that a predicted breach authorizes an arbitrary production change.

steps.phase: Frame the SLO contract and user surfaces
steps.title: Collect standardized SLI telemetry
steps.content: Use an OpenTelemetry-compatible collection tier to normalize service identity, timestamps, and metric samples before buffering them. Measure end-to-end freshness at this boundary against the under-one-minute objective; the brief does not specify a percentile or source clock policy.

component.label: SLI Telemetry Collectors
component.description: Horizontally scalable collection and normalization workers accept standardized service telemetry, attach service/team context, and publish timestamped SLI observations.

properties.purpose: Horizontally scalable collection and normalization workers accept standardized service telemetry, attach service/team context, and publish timestamped SLI observations.

component.highlightReason: A distinct collection boundary lets ingestion freshness and backpressure be measured independently from forecast computation.

steps.phase: Frame the SLO contract and user surfaces
steps.title: Give operators a live compliance surface
steps.content: Provide a dashboard for current SLI status, remaining budget by window, forecast confidence, service/team ownership, and report access. Real-time means the displayed freshness is visible and measured, not that every downstream query is synchronous.

component.label: SLO Operations Dashboard
component.description: Operator and customer-facing views show freshness, service/team compliance, multi-window error budgets, forecast confidence, and access-controlled reports.

properties.purpose: Operator and customer-facing views show freshness, service/team compliance, multi-window error budgets, forecast confidence, and access-controlled reports.

component.highlightReason: The explicit real-time dashboard target needs a user-visible freshness indicator and an observable update path.

steps.phase: Define, ingest, and evaluate SLIs
steps.title: Expose an authenticated SLO API
steps.content: Put authentication, tenant isolation, input validation, and rate controls at the interface used by the dashboard and integrations. Keep the SLO definition API separate from bulk telemetry ingestion so policy changes do not contend with the high-volume path.

component.label: SLO API Gateway
component.description: Authenticated and rate-controlled API boundary for SLO definition management, dashboard queries, reporting requests, and approved integrations.

properties.purpose: Authenticated and rate-controlled API boundary for SLO definition management, dashboard queries, reporting requests, and approved integrations.

component.highlightReason: A single governed API boundary protects tenant data and keeps user queries distinct from telemetry ingestion.

steps.phase: Define, ingest, and evaluate SLIs
steps.title: Keep a versioned SLO control plane
steps.content: Validate SLO definitions, ownership, indicator expressions, service-chain references, and effective dates. Changes should be versioned and auditable; an evaluator must know which definition was active for each observation and report.

component.label: SLO Control Plane
component.description: Validates and versions SLO definitions, ownership, service-chain references, access policy, and report requests; publishes definition changes without coupling them to metric ingestion.

properties.purpose: Validates and versions SLO definitions, ownership, service-chain references, access policy, and report requests; publishes definition changes without coupling them to metric ingestion.

component.highlightReason: Versioned configuration is necessary to explain historical compliance and composite-SLA membership.

steps.phase: Define, ingest, and evaluate SLIs
steps.title: Persist SLO definitions and chain membership
steps.content: Store at least the stated 500 definitions without assuming a particular tenant count or database engine. Keep revision history, service/team ownership, objective, indicator, and the member services and composition rule for each composite SLA.

component.label: SLO and Service-Chain Registry
component.description: Versioned definitions for individual and composite SLOs, service-chain membership, indicator expressions, ownership, effective dates, and audit history; sizing beyond 500+ definitions is workload-dependent.

properties.purpose: Versioned definitions for individual and composite SLOs, service-chain membership, indicator expressions, ownership, effective dates, and audit history; sizing beyond 500+ definitions is workload-dependent.

component.highlightReason: The registry makes the 500-definition and composite-SLA requirements explicit without selecting an unstated vendor or capacity target.

steps.phase: Define, ingest, and evaluate SLIs
steps.title: Buffer observations and definition updates
steps.content: Use a durable event stream to decouple telemetry collection from calculation and to replay after consumer failure. Partitioning, retention, and ordering keys require the missing workload and tenant details; preserve event timestamps and definition revisions in each event.

component.label: SLI and SLO Event Stream
component.description: Durable stream carrying timestamped SLI observations and versioned SLO-definition changes to independent evaluation, forecast, and reporting consumers.

properties.purpose: Durable stream carrying timestamped SLI observations and versioned SLO-definition changes to independent evaluation, forecast, and reporting consumers.

component.highlightReason: A replayable buffer absorbs bursts and isolates the minute-level freshness objective from downstream work.

steps.phase: Define, ingest, and evaluate SLIs
steps.title: Evaluate burn and budgets for each window
steps.content: Compute indicator compliance, burn rate, and remaining error budget continuously for the required hourly, daily, and monthly windows. Make late data, resets, and changes to an SLO definition explicit so the dashboard does not silently mix revisions.

component.label: SLI and Error-Budget Evaluator
component.description: Streaming evaluator calculates SLI status, burn rates, remaining budgets for hourly/daily/monthly windows, and composite service-chain compliance from versioned definitions.

properties.purpose: Streaming evaluator calculates SLI status, burn rates, remaining budgets for hourly/daily/monthly windows, and composite service-chain compliance from versioned definitions.

component.highlightReason: Burn-rate evaluation and explicit windows turn raw telemetry into the continuously updated budgets required by the brief.

steps.phase: Define, ingest, and evaluate SLIs
steps.title: Retain queryable history for budgets and forecasts
steps.content: Persist time-series aggregates and the provenance needed to reconstruct budget and forecast inputs. Hot retention and resolution are not specified here; preserve enough history for the agreed prediction horizon and later accuracy evaluation, then size storage from measured volume.

component.label: SLI Time-Series Store
component.description: Queryable time-series observations and aggregates with event-time, service/team, SLO revision, and window provenance for current budgets, forecasts, reports, and evaluation.

properties.purpose: Queryable time-series observations and aggregates with event-time, service/team, SLO revision, and window provenance for current budgets, forecasts, reports, and evaluation.

component.highlightReason: Historical evidence is needed for forecasts and reports; retention and resolution must be agreed rather than invented.

steps.phase: Define, ingest, and evaluate SLIs
steps.title: Train forecasts against time-correct outcomes
steps.content: Build training data from historical SLI windows and subsequently observed breaches, split by time, and avoid using post-forecast data as a feature. Define the greater-than-90% accuracy metric, horizon-specific cohort, class balance, and confidence calibration before model acceptance.

component.label: Breach Forecast Training
component.description: Reproducible offline pipeline trains and evaluates breach forecasts on time-correct historical windows, with horizon-specific holdouts, label checks, calibration, and versioned evaluation evidence.

properties.purpose: Reproducible offline pipeline trains and evaluates breach forecasts on time-correct historical windows, with horizon-specific holdouts, label checks, calibration, and versioned evaluation evidence.

component.highlightReason: A numeric accuracy target is only meaningful with a defined label, horizon, cohort, and leakage-free test set.

steps.phase: Define, ingest, and evaluate SLIs
steps.title: Serve calibrated breach forecasts
steps.content: Return a breach probability or risk band, forecast horizon, confidence, model version, and input freshness. Missing or stale data should lower confidence or produce an unavailable prediction, never be silently interpreted as healthy.

component.label: SLA Breach Forecaster
component.description: Versioned model forecasts SLA breach risk 1–4 hours ahead and returns calibrated confidence, model provenance, and input-freshness context.

properties.purpose: Versioned model forecasts SLA breach risk 1–4 hours ahead and returns calibrated confidence, model provenance, and input-freshness context.

component.highlightReason: Forecasts augment observed burn rates; confidence and freshness prevent uncertain predictions from being presented as facts.

steps.phase: Define, ingest, and evaluate SLIs
steps.title: Gate mitigations through policy
steps.content: Keep mitigation separate from prediction. Apply an explicit policy using service ownership, confidence, current budget, action allowlists, deduplication, and an auditable approval/rollback path; production actions remain opt-in until their safety criteria are agreed.

component.label: Alert and Mitigation Policy
component.description: Routes observed or predicted breaches to alerts and narrowly allowlisted mitigations, applying confidence thresholds, ownership, deduplication, approvals, and an auditable rollback path.

properties.purpose: Routes observed or predicted breaches to alerts and narrowly allowlisted mitigations, applying confidence thresholds, ownership, deduplication, approvals, and an auditable rollback path.

component.highlightReason: A model prediction is evidence for policy, not permission to change a service automatically.

steps.phase: Define, ingest, and evaluate SLIs
steps.title: Build customer-ready compliance reports
steps.content: Aggregate compliance by SLO revision, service, team, and reporting period, retaining the evidence and freshness that support each result. Apply customer/tenant authorization before export and distinguish measured results from forecasted risk.

component.label: Compliance Reporting
component.description: Produces access-controlled compliance summaries by customer, service, team, SLO revision, and reporting period, preserving evidence lineage and separating observed compliance from forecasts.

properties.purpose: Produces access-controlled compliance summaries by customer, service, team, SLO revision, and reporting period, preserving evidence lineage and separating observed compliance from forecasts.

component.highlightReason: Customer reports need traceable observations and SLO versions, not just the latest dashboard value.

steps.phase: Connect the measurement and prediction path
steps.title: Collect service observations
steps.content: Services emit timestamped measurements and stable service/team identity. Keep the observation contract independent of the evaluator so new services can be onboarded without changing budget logic.

connection.label: Timestamped SLI observations
connection.description: Standardized measurements with event time and service/team identity; exact signal volume remains to be established.

steps.phase: Connect the measurement and prediction path
steps.title: Buffer normalized telemetry
steps.content: Collectors publish normalized observations to the durable stream. Monitor lag and dropped/duplicate events because freshness and correctness both affect the one-minute monitoring objective.

connection.label: Normalized SLI events
connection.description: Replayable observations retain event time, source, service/team, and schema version.

steps.phase: Connect the measurement and prediction path
steps.title: Drive continuous budget evaluation
steps.content: The evaluator consumes telemetry asynchronously and applies the active, versioned SLO definition. Idempotent event handling and late-data policy are part of correctness, not merely throughput tuning.

connection.label: Ordered-by-key SLI events
connection.description: Consumers track offsets and replay safely; ordering and partition keys are chosen after workload discovery.

steps.phase: Connect the measurement and prediction path
steps.title: Submit dashboard actions through the API
steps.content: Dashboard users manage SLOs and query status only through the authenticated interface; never allow a browser to access the registry or telemetry stores directly.

connection.label: Authenticated SLO and status requests
connection.description: Tenant-scoped requests for definitions, compliance, forecasts, and report access.

steps.phase: Connect the measurement and prediction path
steps.title: Route validated requests to the control plane
steps.content: The gateway enforces identity and request limits before the control plane validates definitions and authorizes integrations.

connection.label: Validated SLO operations
connection.description: Versioned requests carry tenant, actor, authorization context, and correlation ID.

steps.phase: Connect the measurement and prediction path
steps.title: Persist and retrieve versioned definitions
steps.content: The control plane records definition changes and resolves the correct revision for evaluation and reporting. Use an explicit definition-change event rather than a hidden cache invalidation assumption.

connection.label: Versioned SLO and chain definitions
connection.description: Validated revisions, ownership, effective dates, composite members, and audit records.

steps.phase: Connect the measurement and prediction path
steps.title: Notify evaluators when definitions change
steps.content: Publish definition revisions so consumers can refresh safely and record which policy was applied to each window. Do not block telemetry collection while a definition is edited.

connection.label: SLO revision events
connection.description: Auditable change notifications identify the new definition revision and effective time.

steps.phase: Connect the measurement and prediction path
steps.title: Resolve the active SLO definition
steps.content: The evaluator reads the applicable version and composite membership for each event-time window; a missing definition should surface as an evaluation error, not a healthy SLO.

connection.label: Active SLO definitions
connection.description: Versioned indicator, objective, owner, time window, and service-chain composition.

steps.phase: Connect the measurement and prediction path
steps.title: Persist evaluated budgets and provenance
steps.content: Write windowed compliance and budget updates with input and definition provenance so the current view and later audit agree.

connection.label: Windowed SLI and budget results
connection.description: Hourly, daily, and monthly aggregates, burn rates, event-time watermarks, and SLO revision references.

steps.phase: Connect the measurement and prediction path
steps.title: Evaluate forecasts on historical windows
steps.content: Training consumes historical inputs and later verified outcomes using time-based splits. Keep labels and evaluation evidence versioned so accuracy claims can be reproduced.

connection.label: Time-correct history and outcomes
connection.description: Historical windows, forecast-time feature snapshots, and verified later breach labels.

steps.phase: Connect the measurement and prediction path
steps.title: Promote evaluated model versions
steps.content: Only a model version that passes the agreed horizon-specific evaluation and confidence calibration is made available to online inference.

connection.label: Validated forecast model artifact
connection.description: Versioned model plus evaluation metadata, calibrated confidence, and supported forecast horizons.

steps.phase: Connect the measurement and prediction path
steps.title: Supply recent budgets and features to inference
steps.content: Recent window aggregates provide burn and budget context. Enforce point-in-time reads so the prediction does not consume data that arrived after its stated forecast time.

connection.label: Fresh budget and SLI features
connection.description: Time-bounded aggregates with explicit source watermark and service/SLO revision.

steps.phase: Connect the measurement and prediction path
steps.title: Forecast risk alongside observed burn
steps.content: The evaluator submits current burn and composite-service context to the forecaster; keep measured violations distinct from predicted future violations.

connection.label: Current burn and chain context
connection.description: Current window status and versioned service-chain features for the 1–4 hour forecast.

steps.phase: Close the mitigation and reporting loop
steps.title: Send forecasts to guarded response policy
steps.content: A forecast reaches response policy with confidence, horizon, model version, and freshness. Low confidence or stale inputs should alert or request review rather than trigger automatic action.

connection.label: Breach risk and confidence
connection.description: Forecast horizon, calibrated confidence, model version, affected services, and freshness metadata.

steps.phase: Close the mitigation and reporting loop
steps.title: Route observed breaches to response policy
steps.content: Observed budget exhaustion can be acted on separately from a forecast. Correlate both paths by service and SLO revision to prevent duplicate pages or actions.

connection.label: Observed breach and burn alerts
connection.description: Current compliance state and evidence for notification or allowlisted mitigation policy.

steps.phase: Close the mitigation and reporting loop
steps.title: Apply only approved service actions
steps.content: The response service invokes a restricted service interface only when policy permits; persist the decision and outcome, and support rollback or human approval where configured.

connection.label: Allowlisted mitigation request
connection.description: Idempotent, scoped action with policy decision, approver context, expiry, and rollback reference.

steps.phase: Close the mitigation and reporting loop
steps.title: Create compliance reports from evaluator output
steps.content: The reporting pipeline consumes evaluated states and forecasts with clear labels for observed versus predicted results.

connection.label: Service and team compliance facts
connection.description: Versioned evaluation outcomes and current status feed report aggregation.

steps.phase: Close the mitigation and reporting loop
steps.title: Include historical evidence in reports
steps.content: Join stored windows to report periods using event time and the relevant SLO revision; preserve the evidence behind customer-visible summaries.

connection.label: Historical compliance evidence
connection.description: Queryable windowed results with service/team attribution and definition provenance.

steps.phase: Close the mitigation and reporting loop
steps.title: Push current status to the dashboard
steps.content: Publish evaluator updates through a push or bounded-refresh channel and expose the last-updated time. Verify end-to-end freshness against the real-time objective under representative load.

connection.label: Live budget and forecast updates
connection.description: Incremental updates include service/SLO identity, observed status, prediction confidence, and freshness timestamp.

steps.phase: Close the mitigation and reporting loop
steps.title: Return authorized views through the control plane
steps.content: The control plane serves the dashboard's definition and report metadata after access checks; it does not bypass the evaluator for current status.

connection.label: Definitions and report metadata
connection.description: Authorized metadata and links to tenant-scoped compliance views.

steps.phase: Close the mitigation and reporting loop
steps.title: Check graph semantics before scoring
steps.content: The online path is service telemetry → collectors → durable events → evaluator → budgets and forecasts → guarded response. The control/report path versions definitions and exposes evidence. If telemetry is delayed, definitions are missing, or confidence is inadequate, surface uncertainty instead of presenting a healthy status.

steps.phase: Close the mitigation and reporting loop
steps.title: Turn each numeric target into a test
steps.content: Load-test with at least the stated 500 definitions and all three windows; measure source-to-dashboard freshness against one minute, and evaluate the stated accuracy on a time-separated, agreed cohort. Report precision/recall or the selected metric, calibration, and confidence intervals rather than asserting a pass from architecture alone.

steps.phase: Close the mitigation and reporting loop
steps.title: Review assumptions with the interviewer
steps.content: Confirm traffic and burst shape, tenant isolation, retention, SLO expression semantics, the forecast accuracy definition, confidence thresholds, mitigation allowlists, and dashboard freshness measurement. Those answers decide sizing and policy; none is silently assumed by this draft.
